hints: Find circle centre $C(3, -2)$ and gradient of radius $CP = \frac{4 - (-2)}{5 - 3} = 3$.
Find tangent gradient $-\frac{1}{3}$ and form tangent equation $x + 3y = 17$.
walkthrough:
Complete the square on the circle equation to locate the centre $C$:
$$(x - 3)^2 - 9 + (y + 2)^2 - 4 - 27 = 0 \implies (x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 40 \implies C(3, -2)$$

Calculate the gradient of the radius joining $C(3, -2)$ to $P(5, 4)$:
$$m_{CP} = \frac{4 - (-2)}{5 - 3} = \frac{6}{2} = 3$$

Determine the gradient and equation of the tangent at $P(5, 4)$:
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{1}{3}$$
$$y - 4 = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 5) \implies 3y - 12 = -x + 5 \implies x + 3y = 17$$

Find the axis intercepts $A$ and $B$:
$$\text{At } y = 0: \quad x = 17 \implies A(17, 0)$$
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad 3y = 17 \implies y = \frac{17}{3} \implies B\left(0, \frac{17}{3}\right)$$

Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle $\triangle OAB$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle OAB) = \frac{1}{2} \times OA \times OB = \frac{1}{2} \times 17 \times \frac{17}{3} = \frac{289}{6} \quad \left(\text{or } 48\frac{1}{6}\right)$$

hints: The radius of the circumcircle is $R = \sqrt{40}$.
Split equilateral $\triangle PQR$ into 3 isosceles triangles with central angle $120^\circ$.
walkthrough: Identify the circumradius $R = \sqrt{40}$ of the circle containing the equilateral triangle $\triangle PQR$.

Divide the equilateral triangle into $3$ congruent isosceles triangles meeting at the circumcentre $C$, each with central angle $\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3} = 120^\circ$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{one triangle}) = \frac{1}{2} R^2 \sin(120^\circ) = \frac{1}{2}(40)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 10\sqrt{3}$$

Multiply by $3$ to find the exact area of the complete equilateral triangle $\triangle PQR$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle PQR) = 3 \times 10\sqrt{3} = 30\sqrt{3} \quad (\approx 51.96)$$
